_comment: The technical track of a general two-day DPI-H for Health workshop: seven modules (T1-T7). Each module is paired with the policy module whose question it serves; each names the journey steps it teaches from, with the technical point there and a technical question for the room. Leads are roles, not people; times are a suggested timetable a host adapts. tools/workshop/module-pages.ts turns this file, schedule.json and policy-agenda.json into the journeys viewer's technical-track workshop (technical-track.workshop.json); tools/workshop/module-journey-map.ts reads it too.
title: Technical track schedule
promise: Two days, one cross-border immunization story. Day 1 covers the building blocks and gets everyone running on Heropa. Day 2 is teams building one part of the journey, then seeing it all work together.

1.summary: Concepts and the OHS stack. By the end of the day you have captured data, synced it, run a workflow and started a dashboard, all on Heropa.

2.summary: Teams build one app in the journey, show it, and then everything runs together.

modules.title: Building with FHIR and the Open Health Stack
modules.carries: Which FHIR resources, terminologies and tools carry this journey, and where does each lab use them?

sessions.title: Talk 1: Building with FHIR and the Open Health Stack
sessions.what: A developer's tour of FHIR, then of the tools around it: the HAPI FHIR server, other open global goods, and where the OHS libraries and the OHS Player fit.

outcomes: Name the FHIR resources you will use over the two days and say what each is for
Explain how terminologies and implementation guides keep data meaningful
Say which parts of the stack each lab uses

steps.technical: Patient and Immunization in the hospital record; each dose signed as a DVC (HCERT).
steps.question: Which FHIR resources does the hospital write for a birth dose, and which of their fields end up in the signed card?

steps.technical: ConceptMap from the product codes of Taifafeki to the schedule codes of Onesa; the schedule as a PlanDefinition.
steps.question: How does an implementation guide let two countries keep their own vaccine codes and still count each other's doses?

steps.technical: The IPS as a FHIR document Bundle assembled from the national record.
steps.question: What makes the IPS readable in another country's system without a bilateral agreement?

modules.title: Offline data capture
modules.carries: How does a form on a health worker's phone become a patient record, with no signal?

sessions.title: Lab 1: Offline data capture
sessions.what: The stack is already running on Heropa. Open a questionnaire in the form editor, change it, and watch the change appear in the OHS Player in your browser. Then add a validation rule or a skip rule. If time allows, see how the answers turn into FHIR resources. Optional: a QR code for the gallery app, to try the same forms on iOS or Android.

outcomes: Edit a FHIR Questionnaire and see the result straight away
Add a validation or skip rule
Describe how captured answers become patient records

steps.technical: The CHW app decodes the paper cards (read-unverified) and fills the form from them, without checking signatures.
steps.question: Which data elements can the form take from a scanned card, and how does it mark them as reported, not verified?

steps.technical: The household registration Questionnaire; answers become Patient, Group (household) and reported Immunization, queued offline.
steps.question: Which validation or skip rule stops a duplicate child being registered in the same household?

modules.title: Trust between countries: SMART Trust and the GDHCN
modules.carries: How can a clinic in one country trust a vaccination record from another, and when is a card better than a link?

sessions.title: Talk 2: Trust between countries, SMART Trust and the GDHCN
sessions.what: How a clinic in one country can trust a vaccination record from another. Covers the GDHCN network, digital vaccine certificates (DVC) and verifiable health links (VHL), and when to use a card and when to use a link.

outcomes: Explain what the GDHCN is and why a verifier needs a trust list
Tell a DVC from a VHL and say when each one fits
Know which parts you will work with on Day 2

steps.technical: The document signer key of Taifafeki (DSC of XXR) signs each DVC as a CWT in COSE.
steps.question: What does the DVC carry, and what does it deliberately leave out, so a card is enough without an identity document?

steps.technical: The clinic verifies each card offline against its cached copy of the GDHCN trust list, by kid.
steps.question: How fresh does the cached trust list have to be, and what should the app show when a signature fails?

steps.technical: The viewer verifies the VHL's HCERT against the DSC of Onesa (XXU) before it fetches anything.
steps.question: Why is the health data not in the QR, and what does the viewer check before it opens the link?

modules.title: Workflows, sync and who sees what
modules.carries: What should happen next for this child, how does the record reach the server, and who is allowed to see it?

sessions.title: Talk 3: Workflows, sync and who sees what
sessions.what: A short briefing before Lab 2. A plan definition says what should happen and when, such as the next vaccine due. Sync moves records between the device and the server. The gateway decides which records each user can reach.

sessions.title: Lab 2: Sync data and run a workflow
sessions.what: In the Player, store records on the device and sync them to the server. Apply an immunization plan definition and see what comes due. Then sign in as two different users through the gateway and compare what each can see, for example 50 records against 10.

outcomes: Sync records between the Player and the FHIR server
Read a plan definition and follow it through a workflow
Show that the gateway filters records by user

steps.technical: Everything Vilay records stays queued on the phone, for up to 28 days, and syncs when a signal returns.
steps.question: What happens to a queued registration if the clinic registers the same child before the phone syncs?

steps.technical: The Onesa schedule (PlanDefinition) runs over every dose; at 10 weeks the 6-week doses come out overdue.
steps.question: How does the plan definition decide a dose is overdue, and what sets the date of the next one?

steps.technical: The family's consent is recorded before the portal issues the link; the gateway enforces passcode, expiry and consent on every request.
steps.question: Where does the gateway read the consent from, and what does it do when the link has expired?

steps.technical: Each view is logged as an AuditEvent in Onesa, including failed passcode attempts.
steps.question: Which AuditEvent fields let Onesa tell the family who looked at the record, and when?

modules.title: From records to charts
modules.carries: How does a FHIR record become a row, a chart and a coverage number, and who accessed what?

sessions.title: Talk 4: From records to charts
sessions.what: How data gets out of the FHIR server and into tables you can chart. A look at FHIR Data Pipes, how one resource becomes a row, and what a dashboard reads.

sessions.title: Lab 3: Build your first dashboard
sessions.what: A guided start in class, then a take-home task. Look at a dashboard built on the data from Lab 2. Add a small batch of new records, run the pipeline again and watch the chart update. Look at the audit events to see who accessed what. You then have about 24 hours to finish a dashboard of your own.

outcomes: Describe the path from a FHIR resource to a chart
Run the pipeline and see new data appear on a chart
Read the audit events for who accessed which record
Finish a simple dashboard of your own

steps.technical: A child born abroad and registered at home enters the coverage denominator here.
steps.question: Which flattened table and which column put Somsak in the coverage denominator, and when?

steps.technical: Verified doses, including those given abroad, count toward coverage indicators.
steps.question: How does the indicator count a dose given abroad without counting it twice?

steps.technical: AuditEvents become an access log you can chart.
steps.question: What would a 'who looked at this child's record abroad' chart need from the AuditEvent rows?

modules.title: Verifying a card, sharing a link
modules.carries: How does an app go from a scanned QR to a verified result, and from a shared link to the records behind it?

sessions.title: Talk 5: Verifying a card, sharing a link, and what you build today
sessions.what: The trust ideas from Day 1 in practice. How an app reads a vaccination QR and checks it against the trust list, and how a shared health link is opened. Then a look at the four pieces the teams will build.

outcomes: Follow a card from scan to verified result
Follow a health link from QR to records
Pick the team you will join

steps.technical: Scan, Base45 and zlib decode, COSE signature check against the trust list, then import with provenance.
steps.question: At which step of decoding does a tampered card fail, and what does the nurse see?

steps.technical: The portal encrypts the IPS and DVCs, publishes a manifest and signs the link as an HCERT.
steps.question: What is inside the link QR, and why can a 4-digit passcode be enough?

steps.technical: The viewer fetches the manifest with an HTTP Message Signature, sends the passcode, and decrypts the documents.
steps.question: What does the viewer need from the trust list, and what does it need from the gateway of Onesa?

modules.title: Team build, showcase and the journey together
modules.carries: Can each team change one app in the journey and then run the whole journey live, from a birth abroad to a clinic back home to the family travelling again?

sessions.title: Team build, part 1
sessions.what: Each team takes one app in the journey. Everything is pre-configured, so there is no Android Studio. You run the app, read how its configuration works, and change it. Test with the vaccination cards.

sessions.title: Team build, part 2
sessions.what: Finish the change, test it with the cards, and get ready to show it.

sessions.title: Team presentations
sessions.what: Each team shows what it built, about seven minutes each. Volunteers present.

sessions.title: Putting the journey together
sessions.what: Volunteers run the whole journey on the demo system, each using their own piece. This is the rehearsal for the finale.

outcomes: Run your app and find where its configuration lives
Make one change and see it work
Have a working piece you can show in under seven minutes

teams.name: CHW app
teams.what: Scan a vaccination card, add the child to the household, and refer them to a clinic.

teams.name: Clinic app
teams.what: Receive the referral, verify the card against the trust list, and plan the next visit.

teams.name: Family app
teams.what: Hold the family's records and share a child's record as a health link.

teams.name: Viewer app
teams.what: Open a shared health link and read the records behind it.

steps.technical: CHW app team: the registration form, the household, the referral.
steps.question: Which one configuration change would make the CHW app fit your country's household register?

steps.technical: Clinic app team: the verifier and its trust store.
steps.question: How would your clinic app load your country's trust list, and how often would it refresh it?

steps.technical: Family app team: one phone, one profile and one link per member.
steps.question: How should the family app separate each member's records on a shared phone?

steps.technical: Viewer app team: open the link, enter the passcode, read the records.
steps.question: What must the viewer show the clinician about where the records came from?

joint.title: FHIR around the world and the story we follow
joint.leads: Workshop hosts, with the policy track

joint.title: What we did today
joint.leads: Lead facilitator for the technical track

joint.title: The journey live, readouts and next steps
joint.leads: Lead facilitator with the workshop hosts

prepare: Agree the joint sessions on both days with the policy track, and who leads each closing slot.
Test the hosted classroom environment (Heropa) the week before. Day 2 apps need an emulator or the Wasm web build, since nobody installs Android Studio.
Lab 3: set up the dashboard tooling and the shared test data, with help on hand once the apps are seeded.
Assign a facilitator to each Day 2 team.
Record the full journey once as a fallback for the finale.
